title: Czech Master English Test Practice 2
source: Czech Master English Test Practice 2 — a new 100-item set (50 grammar, 50 vocabulary) written to mirror the topics of the original Master Scholarship English placement test, from the internet.

groups.instruction: Choose the option that best completes each sentence.

questions.prompt: She _______ in this city for over ten years.
questions.explanation: "For over ten years" describes a duration continuing up to now, which the present perfect expresses: "has lived".

questions.prompt: We _______ each other since we graduated.
questions.explanation: "Since" marks a starting point for an action continuing up to now, matching the present perfect "haven't seen".

questions.prompt: By the time you arrive, I _______ dinner.
questions.explanation: "By the time" plus a future event marks an action completed before that point, which the future perfect expresses: "will have cooked".

questions.prompt: As soon as the rain _______, we'll leave.
questions.explanation: A time clause introduced by "as soon as" that refers to the future uses the present simple, "stops", not a future or continuous form.

questions.prompt: He asked me if I _______ Mary.
questions.explanation: In reported speech, a present-tense question backshifts to the past when the reporting verb is past, giving "if I knew Mary".

questions.prompt: She wondered whether he _______ coming to the party.
questions.explanation: Reported speech about an ongoing situation backshifts the present continuous to the past continuous, "was coming", matching the past reporting verb "wondered".

questions.prompt: I wish I _______ harder for the exam last month.
questions.explanation: A wish about a specific past event, "last month", takes the past perfect, "had studied", to express regret about something that didn't happen.

questions.prompt: He talks as if he _______ everything already.
questions.explanation: "As if" introducing an unreal comparison about the present takes the past simple, "knew", similar to a second conditional.

questions.prompt: You _______ have told me earlier — now it's too late.
questions.explanation: "Should have + past participle" expresses criticism of a past action that didn't happen, matching the regret that "now it's too late".

questions.prompt: I _______ finish this report before noon; it's non-negotiable.
questions.explanation: "Must" expresses strong, non-negotiable obligation, matching the follow-up "it's non-negotiable".

questions.prompt: She _______ rather stay home than go to the party.
questions.explanation: "Would rather" expresses a preference and is followed by the bare infinitive "stay".

questions.prompt: You _______ better see a doctor about that cough.
questions.explanation: "Had better" is the fixed modal expression for strong advice, followed by the bare infinitive "see".

questions.prompt: He will never _______ them to cancel the trip.
questions.explanation: "Allow someone to do something" fits refusing to permit an action. "Admit" means confess, and "tolerate"/"let" don't take a to-infinitive in this pattern.

questions.prompt: One more mistake won't do any _______.
questions.explanation: "Do any harm" is the fixed collocation for causing damage. "Hurt", "bad", and "ill" don't fit this exact phrase.

questions.prompt: If _______ I had listened to her advice!
questions.explanation: "If only" is the fixed exclamatory structure for wishing something in the past had been different.

questions.prompt: _______ I open the window for you?
questions.explanation: "Shall I...?" is the standard way to offer to do something for someone, unlike "Do you want that I" or "Would you like that I", which are not natural English structures.

questions.prompt: If I _______ rich, I would travel the world.
questions.explanation: A second conditional describing a hypothetical present uses "were" in the if-clause, paired with "would travel" in the main clause.

questions.prompt: Had I known the truth, I _______ differently.
questions.explanation: "Had I known" is an inverted third conditional if-clause (equivalent to "If I had known"), which needs "would have acted" in the main clause.

questions.prompt: The passengers were _______ to remain seated during turbulence.
questions.explanation: "Advised to do something" fits a safety recommendation given to passengers. "Informed" would need a fact stated rather than an instruction, and "suggested" cannot take a personal object plus infinitive this way.

questions.prompt: She had her car _______ last week.
questions.explanation: "Have something done" is the causative pattern for work carried out by someone else, and the car receives the repairing, so the past participle "repaired" is required.

questions.prompt: The new policy was strongly _______ by the committee.
questions.explanation: "Strongly recommended" is the natural collocation for an emphatic proposal put forward by a group.

questions.prompt: He is said _______ the fastest runner in school.
questions.explanation: "Is said to be" is the fixed passive reporting structure for describing what people say about someone, using the to-infinitive.

questions.prompt: She bought _______ new shoes for the wedding.
questions.explanation: Shoes naturally come as a matched pair, so "a pair of shoes" is the natural way to count one set, rather than the singular "a" or "a couple"/"two of".

questions.prompt: The committee _______ twelve members.
questions.explanation: "Consist of" is the correct fixed verb-preposition pairing for describing what makes up a group. "Composes of" is not standard, and "consists in" means something different (to lie in an abstract quality).

questions.prompt: I haven't got the _______ idea what he's talking about.
questions.explanation: "Haven't got the faintest idea" is a fixed idiom meaning having no idea at all.

questions.prompt: _______ of the students passed the final exam.
questions.explanation: "None of" is the correct negative quantifier for saying that not a single student passed. "Anyone"/"someone" don't fit this negative meaning.

questions.prompt: There isn't _______ milk left in the fridge.
questions.explanation: "Milk" is uncountable, and a negative statement about quantity uses "much", not the countable quantifiers "many"/"a few"/"several".

questions.prompt: She has _______ furniture in her new apartment.
questions.explanation: "Furniture" is uncountable, and the negative sense (an almost-empty apartment) needs "little", not "a few"/"a number of", which pair with countable nouns.

questions.prompt: Jealousy _______ his is dangerous.
questions.explanation: This elliptical comparison uses "as", meaning "jealousy such as his". "Similar than" is ungrammatical, and "the same as" would need a different sentence structure.

questions.prompt: He behaves _______ his father did at that age.
questions.explanation: "Like" is used before a noun/clause to express similarity in behaviour, matching "he behaves like his father did". "Similar than" is not grammatical, and "the same that" is not standard.

questions.prompt: The outcome is _______ to disappoint everyone.
questions.explanation: "Likely to be" is the fixed pattern for describing a probable outcome, using the adjective "likely". "Probably" is an adverb needing a different sentence structure.

questions.prompt: This model is twice _______ expensive as that one.
questions.explanation: "Twice as ... as" is the fixed multiple-comparison pattern. "More", "so", and "such" don't complete this exact structure.

questions.prompt: The keys were found in the _______.
questions.explanation: "Nearest" describes physical proximity, fitting a location description, while "next" would imply a sequence. "Car park" is the standard noun; "parking" alone is not used as a place noun this way.

questions.prompt: She learned the whole poem _______ heart.
questions.explanation: "Learn something by heart" is the fixed idiom for memorising it exactly.

questions.prompt: He searched _______ vain for his passport.
questions.explanation: "In vain" is the fixed idiom for an effort that has no result.

questions.prompt: This is _______ no means an easy task.
questions.explanation: "By no means" is the fixed idiom meaning "not at all".

questions.prompt: That was a comment from the review, in _______ you weren't aware.
questions.explanation: "In case you weren't aware" is the fixed phrase for adding information the listener might not already have.

questions.prompt: Her voice always reminds me _______ my grandmother.
questions.explanation: "Remind someone of someone/something" is the fixed verb-preposition pairing for triggering a memory or association.

questions.prompt: He'll manage on his own _______ the time being.
questions.explanation: "For the time being" is the fixed phrase meaning "for now, temporarily".

questions.prompt: _______ as I can recall, the shop has always been here.
questions.explanation: "As far as I can recall" is the fixed phrase for qualifying a statement based on the limits of one's memory. "As long" relates to duration or condition, not memory limits.

questions.prompt: He paused in _______ to catch his breath.
questions.explanation: "Pause in order to do something" expresses purpose, matching "to catch his breath".

questions.prompt: He did it _______ purpose, just to annoy her.
questions.explanation: "On purpose" is the fixed idiom meaning "intentionally", matching "just to annoy her".

questions.prompt: The decision is _______, not mine.
questions.explanation: A possessive pronoun standing alone after a linking verb needs the independent form, "hers", not the possessive adjective "her" or the reflexive "herself".

questions.prompt: That is _______ really matters in the end.
questions.explanation: "What" functions as a nominal relative pronoun meaning "the thing that", correctly standing alone without a following noun.

questions.prompt: She traveled all _______ across Europe last summer.
questions.explanation: "By herself" is the fixed idiom meaning "alone, without company".

questions.prompt: His latest novel sounds _______.
questions.explanation: "Sound" here is a linking verb describing an impression, taking the plain adjective "great", not an adverb or an infinitive/gerund phrase.

questions.prompt: They left the building _______.
questions.explanation: "In a hurry" is the fixed idiomatic phrase for doing something quickly, using the indefinite article "a".

questions.prompt: I hope you slept well _______.
questions.explanation: "Slept" is past tense, which needs a matching past time expression, "last night", not "tonight"/"this night", which refer to the present or future.

questions.prompt: He couldn't decide _______ accept the job offer.
questions.explanation: "Deciding whether to do something" is the fixed pattern for expressing a choice between two options using a to-infinitive.

questions.prompt: I was so nervous I asked _______ to speak on my behalf.
questions.explanation: "Someone else" is the fixed pattern for referring to an unspecified additional person.

groups.instruction: Choose the option that best completes each sentence.

questions.prompt: The negotiations have completely _______ steam.
questions.explanation: "Run out of steam" is the fixed idiom for losing momentum or energy.

questions.prompt: We're going to _______ money if we keep spending like this.
questions.explanation: "Run out of money" means to have none left, using the same phrasal verb pattern as "run out of steam".

questions.prompt: Fighting _______ between the two rival gangs last night.
questions.explanation: "Break out" is the fixed phrasal verb for violence or conflict starting suddenly.

questions.prompt: The meeting _______ into chaos after the announcement.
questions.explanation: "Broke up" describes a meeting falling apart or ending in disorder, here "into chaos" after the announcement, distinct from "broke out", used for conflicts or wars suddenly starting.

questions.prompt: War _______ shortly after the treaty collapsed.
questions.explanation: "Break out" is the fixed phrasal verb for a war starting suddenly.

questions.prompt: They had to _______ with the delays at the airport.
questions.explanation: "Put up with" means to tolerate something unpleasant, matching enduring delays.

questions.prompt: She _______ for her earlier rudeness by apologizing sincerely.
questions.explanation: "Make up for something" means to compensate for a past wrong, matching apologizing to make amends for rudeness.

questions.prompt: The accident put him _______ driving for months.
questions.explanation: "Put someone off doing something" means to discourage them from continuing it, fitting an accident discouraging someone from driving.

questions.prompt: It took her years to learn how to _______ a motorcycle properly.
questions.explanation: "Ride a motorcycle" is the fixed collocation for that activity. "Drive" is used for cars, and "direct"/"conduct" don't fit.

questions.prompt: He decided to _______ smoking once and for all.
questions.explanation: "Give up" means to stop doing a habit permanently, matching "once and for all".

questions.prompt: The company had to _______ off dozens of workers.
questions.explanation: "Lay off" is the fixed phrasal verb for dismissing employees due to lack of work, not "let off"/"take off"/"cut off".

questions.prompt: Please _______ down the volume; the baby is sleeping.
questions.explanation: "Turn down" is the fixed phrasal verb for reducing a setting such as volume.

questions.prompt: She _______ at him briefly before looking away.
questions.explanation: "Glanced" describes a brief, quick look, matching "briefly before looking away". "Glimpsed" describes catching sight of something unintentionally.

questions.prompt: She _______ the chance to study abroad without hesitation.
questions.explanation: "Take a chance/opportunity" is the fixed collocation for seizing it.

questions.prompt: He became _______ to painkillers after the surgery.
questions.explanation: "Addicted to" is the fixed collocation for dependency on a substance.

questions.prompt: I can _______ you that the information is accurate.
questions.explanation: "Assure someone (that)" means to tell them confidently to remove their doubt. "Confirm"/"insist"/"declare" don't take a personal object the same way.

questions.prompt: She didn't want to _______ her neighbors with her problems.
questions.explanation: "Bother someone with something" means to trouble them unnecessarily.

questions.prompt: He _______ to admit that he had made a mistake.
questions.explanation: "Refused to do something" fits declining to act, taking a to-infinitive. "Rejected" would need a direct object, not a to-infinitive.

questions.prompt: Her parents strongly _______ of her decision to drop out.
questions.explanation: "Disapproved of" is the fixed collocation for viewing something negatively. "Condemned" would take a direct object, not "of".

questions.prompt: He _______ a match and lit the candle.
questions.explanation: "Strike a match" is the fixed collocation for lighting one.

questions.prompt: Don't call me a _______ — I'm telling the truth!
questions.explanation: "Liar" describes someone who tells untruths, fitting being accused of dishonesty.

questions.prompt: The news left everyone feeling quite _______.
questions.explanation: "Upset" describes an emotional reaction to distressing news, matching the general context better than "anxious"/"confused"/"discouraged".

questions.prompt: This is my _______ restaurant in the whole city.
questions.explanation: "Favourite" describes a personal preference, fitting "my ... restaurant". "Popular" describes wide appeal to others, not personal preference.

questions.prompt: My main _______ is to finish the project on time.
questions.explanation: "Intention" describes a planned goal, fitting "is to finish the project".

questions.prompt: The printer seems to be out of _______ again.
questions.explanation: "Out of order" is the fixed idiom for something not working properly.

questions.prompt: Roast lamb is my favourite _______ at this restaurant.
questions.explanation: "Dish" refers to a particular type of prepared food. "Plate" refers to tableware, "course" to a stage of a meal, and "menu" to the list of dishes offered.

questions.prompt: Getting through customs took _______.
questions.explanation: "An hour's work" uses the possessive form for a time-based measurement of effort, the standard pattern for this kind of phrase.

questions.prompt: The box was _______ heavy to lift alone.
questions.explanation: "Too + adjective + to-infinitive" expresses that something exceeds an ability, matching "to lift alone".

questions.prompt: Why not try painting, or anything _______ creative?
questions.explanation: "Anything else" is the fixed pattern for referring to additional, unnamed options.

questions.prompt: The holiday season is _______ fast, with shops getting busier.
questions.explanation: "Coming up" describes an event or period approaching in time, fitting a season about to arrive.

questions.prompt: The fault for the delay is entirely _______.
questions.explanation: A possessive pronoun standing alone after a linking verb needs the independent form, "hers".

questions.prompt: That's exactly _______ I meant.
questions.explanation: "What" functions as a nominal relative pronoun meaning "the thing that".

questions.prompt: He lived alone, _______, in a small cottage.
questions.explanation: "By himself" is the fixed idiom meaning "alone, without company".

questions.prompt: The offer sounds too good to be _______.
questions.explanation: "Too good to be true" is the fixed idiom for something that seems unbelievably favourable.

questions.prompt: He apologized _______, clearly embarrassed by his mistake.
questions.explanation: "Apologized" is a verb, which needs an adverb to modify it, "sincerely", not an adjective or a prepositional phrase.

questions.prompt: She was determined to _______ up her own business someday.
questions.explanation: "Set up a business" is the fixed phrasal verb for starting a company.

questions.prompt: He managed to _______ the issue amicably.
questions.explanation: "Settle an issue amicably" is the fixed collocation for resolving a dispute in a friendly way.

questions.prompt: The committee will _______ into the matter thoroughly.
questions.explanation: "Look into a matter" is the fixed phrasal verb for investigating something.

questions.prompt: Please _______ attention to the safety instructions.
questions.explanation: "Pay attention to" is the fixed collocation for focusing on something.

questions.prompt: It's important to _______ a good impression at interviews.
questions.explanation: "Make a good impression" is the fixed collocation for how one is perceived by others.

questions.prompt: The train was two hours _______ because of the storm.
questions.explanation: "Delayed" describes something arriving later than scheduled, fitting a specific time amount ("two hours"). "Cancelled"/"suspended" would mean it didn't run at all.

questions.prompt: He finally _______ his fear of public speaking.
questions.explanation: "Overcome a fear" is the fixed collocation for successfully dealing with it.

questions.prompt: She couldn't _______ her curiosity and opened the letter.
questions.explanation: "Resist curiosity/temptation" is the fixed collocation for holding back from acting on an urge.

questions.prompt: The company plans to _______ its workforce by 20%.
questions.explanation: "Reduce" fits a workforce being cut by a percentage. "Lower" is typically used for prices or levels, not a count of people.

questions.prompt: He was _______ for the position because of his experience.
questions.explanation: "Qualified for a position" is the fixed collocation for having the right skills or credentials.

questions.prompt: The lawyer _______ strongly on behalf of her client.
questions.explanation: "Argued strongly" fits a lawyer making a forceful case. "Discussed"/"talked"/"spoke" don't carry the same sense of advocating a position.

questions.prompt: They had to _______ the risks before making a decision.
questions.explanation: "Weigh the risks" is the fixed collocation for carefully considering pros and cons before deciding.

questions.prompt: The scandal _______ the politician's reputation.
questions.explanation: "Damaged" is the standard collocation for harming an abstract thing like a reputation.

questions.prompt: She _______ great pride in her work.
questions.explanation: "Take pride in something" is the fixed collocation for feeling satisfaction in one's work.

questions.prompt: The new law will come _______ effect next month.
questions.explanation: "Come into effect" is the fixed phrase for a law or rule starting to apply.
